questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has one angle of $40°$. Which of the following could be the other two angles?

options.text: Both A and B are possible

questions.explanation: An isosceles triangle has two equal angles. If the $40°$ angle is one of the equal pair, the angles are $40°$, $40°$, $100°$. If the $40°$ is the unequal angle, the other two are each $\frac{180° - 40°}{2} = 70°$. Both configurations are valid.

questions.stem: In a triangle, one interior angle is $80°$. The exterior angle adjacent to one of the other angles is $130°$. What is the third interior angle of the triangle?
questions.explanation: An exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle are supplementary, so the interior angle next to $130°$ is $180° - 130° = 50°$. The third angle is $180° - 80° - 50° = 50°$. Alternatively, the exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles: $130° = 80° + 50°$.

questions.stem: Each angle in an equilateral triangle measures:
questions.explanation: An equilateral triangle has three equal angles. Since angles in a triangle sum to $180°$, each angle is $\frac{180°}{3} = 60°$.
